title: Space Tech on Earth
objective: After this level you can name everyday technologies that came out of space research.
summary: Phone camera sensors grew from 1990s JPL research and memory foam from 1966 NASA airplane seats. Tang, Teflon and Velcro are not NASA inventions; astronauts just made them famous.

cards.headline: The camera in your phone grew out of a NASA project.
cards.body: NASA calls space technologies that end up in everyday life spinoffs, and it has published a Spinoff report every year since 1976. Some spinoffs are hiding in your pocket and under you right now. Some famous ones aren't spinoffs at all.

cards.headline: A camera on a chip
cards.body: In the 1990s, NASA wanted smaller spacecraft cameras that used less power. Eric Fossum's team at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory built CMOS image sensors: a whole camera on one chip, far smaller and far thriftier with power than the sensors of the day. Small and battery-friendly turned out to be exactly what cell phones needed. Fossum called phones the killer application. The camera built for spacecraft ended up in your pocket.

cards.fact: Memory foam began as an airplane seat cushion in 1966.
cards.context: NASA's Ames Research Center wanted seats that protected people better in a crash. Charles Yost, working with NASA, made a foam that slowly molded to whatever pressed on it, then sprang back once the pressure was gone: "slow spring back foam." Later it padded football helmets, helped prevent bedsores and cushioned shoe insoles.

mascot.line: A crash-safety cushion that ended up in your shoes. Knowledge travels.

cards.headline: Myth check: NASA didn't invent Velcro
cards.body: Some famous "space inventions" aren't. NASA itself says General Foods developed Tang in 1957, DuPont invented Teflon in 1938, and a Swiss engineer invented Velcro in the 1940s. Astronauts made them famous: John Glenn drank Tang in orbit in 1962, and Apollo missions used Velcro to anchor equipment. Using something in space isn't the same as inventing it.

questions.prompt: Which everyday technology grew from a NASA effort to make smaller, low-power spacecraft cameras?

options.label: Velcro
options.rationale: A Swiss engineer invented it in the 1940s.

options.label: The CMOS image sensor in phone cameras

questions.explanation: Eric Fossum's JPL team built CMOS image sensors in the 1990s; cell phones became their killer application.

questions.prompt: Why do so many people think NASA invented Velcro?

options.label: Apollo missions used it to anchor equipment
It was first made aboard a spacecraft
options.rationale: It was invented in the 1940s, on Earth.

options.label: John Glenn invented it in orbit
options.rationale: Glenn drank Tang in orbit; he didn't invent Velcro.

questions.explanation: Velcro was invented in the 1940s; its heavy use on Apollo missions tied it to NASA in people's minds.

options.label: Every NASA product was invented by NASA
Useful inventions must run on electricity
